events.explanation: Goalie outlet reaches the carrier. This is possession, not a scoring chance.
Carrier advances; the middle passing opportunity opens.
Pass reaches the receiving lane but control is not awarded. The assigned receiver must handle it under pressure.
Receiver establishes control and a declared contested-release opportunity opens. No shot or goal is awarded yet.
Shooter gets an on-target release past the assigned gap defender. The shot is in flight; the goalie must respond. No goal yet.
Goalie tracks and stops the clear-view shot. Save contact does not grant control; rebound containment must resolve next.
Rebound containment fails under the assigned receiver's pressure. The window ends with a loose puck, not automatic skater possession or a rebound goal.

scene.note: Authored shooting rules 0.4: controlled reception opens a contested release, receiver Shooting versus assigned gap defender Defending. On-target flight requires away goalie Tracking versus shooter Shooting in a fixed clear-view situation. Save contact stays uncontrolled; goalie Rebounds versus receiver Handling determines held or loose. These sequential contests assert no empirical independence. No extra support on receive/shoot/save/rebound. Release/rebound failures end loose; save failure scores. Ties end unresolved with puck status preserved. No traffic, lateral movement, nearest-player geometry, clock, fatigue, restart or NHL probabilities. Positioning, Movement and Recovery are not tested.
